brand.voiceLine: Earth has bugs. This is one of them.

audience: Curious adults and teens in the USA and UK

niche.primary: Real, verified facts that feel like glitches in Earth's code: bizarre animals and nature, physics and space anomalies, the human body, strange places, history's weird coincidences, and everyday things that make no sense until explained. Frame each topic as a 'bug' in reality, then explain the real science behind it.
avoid: tragedies, violence, crime involving real victims
anything that cannot be backed by at least two reputable sources

kinetic.bestFor: tech, business, money, companies, 'how X works', lists, stats, comparisons

collage.bestFor: psychology, self-improvement, history, culture, ideas, quotes, 'why we do X'

crayon.bestFor: wholesome stories, animals, nature, space for beginners, origins of everyday things, simple science

documentary.bestFor: animals in action, nature, oceans, places, mysteries, events with real-world visuals

blueprint3d.bestFor: engineering, inventions, machines, space hardware, architecture, how a device works inside

mascot.bestFor: fun weird facts, everyday mysteries, 'why does X happen', body facts, light science; the channel's Earth mascot hosts

globe3d.bestFor: places on Earth, geography, migrations, weather, oceans, borders, 'the only place where…', time zones, plate tectonics

newsflash.bestFor: recent discoveries, new studies, space missions, record-breaking events, 'scientists just found…' topics with reputable sources

schedule.timezoneNote: 18:00 UTC = 7pm UK (BST: 7pm, GMT: 6pm) and 2pm New York (EDT) — a strong overlap slot for US+UK.
